translation_en:
Sa'id bin 'Ufair narrated that al-Layth told him, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab: Malik bin Aws bin al-Hadathan informed me. Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mut'im had mentioned to me something from his account, so I went and met Malik bin Aws and asked him about it. Malik said:

I went to see 'Umar. His doorkeeper, Yarfa', came and said, 'Will you receive 'Uthman, 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Zubair, and Sa'd? They are asking permission to enter.' 'Umar said, 'Yes,' and admitted them. They entered, greeted him, and sat down. After a short while Yarfa' came again and said, 'Will you receive 'Ali and al-'Abbas?' 'Umar said, 'Yes,' and admitted them. They entered, greeted him, and sat down. Al-'Abbas said, 'Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this man.' 'Uthman and his companions said, 'Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve one of them of the other.'

'Umar said, 'Wait. I adjure you by Allah, by whose command the heavens and earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "We are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity"? He meant himself.' They replied, 'He did say that.' 'Umar turned to 'Ali and al-'Abbas and said, 'I adjure you by Allah: do you both know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that?' They replied, 'He did say that.'

'Umar continued, 'I will explain this matter to you. Allah granted His Messenger a special share of this property that He granted to no one else. Allah said: "Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur horses or camels for it" (Quran 59:6), and continued to the words, "and Allah is capable of all things." This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). By Allah, he did not take it for himself to the exclusion of you, nor did he keep it for himself instead of you. He gave it to you and distributed it among you, until this property remained. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to provide his family's yearly maintenance from it, then take what remained and put it toward the public treasury. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) followed this practice throughout his life. I adjure you by Allah: do you know this?' They said, 'Yes.' He said to 'Ali and al-'Abbas, 'I adjure you by Allah: do you both know this?' They said, 'Yes.'

Then Allah took His Prophet's life, and Abu Bakr said, 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' Abu Bakr took charge of it and managed it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had managed it. At that time, you—turning to 'Ali and al-'Abbas—claimed that Abu Bakr had done such-and-such. Allah knows that he was truthful, dutiful, rightly guided, and following the truth in this matter.

Then Allah took Abu Bakr's life, and I said, 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of Abu Bakr.' I took charge of it for two years and managed it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr had done. Then both of you came to me, united in what you said and in your purpose: you came asking me for your share from your nephew, and this one came asking me for his wife's share from her father. I said, 'If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you pledge before Allah to manage it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did, as Abu Bakr did, and as I have done since I took charge of it. Otherwise, do not bring this matter to me.' You both said, 'Hand it over to us on that condition,' so I handed it over to you on that condition. I adjure you by Allah: did I hand it over to them on that condition?' The group replied, 'Yes.'

'Umar then turned to 'Ali and al-'Abbas and said, 'I adjure you by Allah: did I hand it over to you on that condition?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Are you now asking me to judge it differently? By the One by whose command the heavens and earth stand, I will never judge this matter differently until the Last Hour comes. If you cannot manage it, then return it to me, and I will take care of it for you.'
